entities.summary:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP — 'Common Man Party') is an Indian political party founded in 2012 by Arvind Kejriwal and anti-corruption activists following the India Against Corruption movement led by Anna Hazare. Rising from civil society protest to governance in under two years, AAP won the 2015 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections with a historic 67 of 70 seats — the most decisive state election result in Indian political history.

AAP emerged from disillusionment with India's two dominant parties — the Indian National Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party — offering a new model of citizen politics, participatory governance, and anti-corruption administration. Kejriwal's administration in Delhi implemented free electricity up to 200 units, free water up to 20,000 liters, and expanded mohalla clinics (neighborhood health centers), making Delhi's governance a case study for other states.

AAP expanded to Punjab, winning the 2022 state elections with 92 of 117 seats, becoming India's first 'national alternative' party to challenge BJP-Congress duopoly in two major states simultaneously. Arvind Kejriwal's March 2024 arrest on corruption charges — involving alleged irregularities in Delhi's liquor policy — created India's most politically charged legal case of the election year, with Kejriwal governing from jail before his conditional release. The case raised questions about the use of investigative agencies as political tools against opposition parties.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: AAP demonstrated that civil society movements can become viable governing parties in the world's largest democracy, winning historic election majorities and creating governance innovations that challenged established political models.
